name: Last Light Hospice Comfort Gown
description:
A soft, weighted gown provided to terminal patients at Last Light Hospice facilities. The gown's weighted fabric provides gentle, distributed pressure — similar to a weighted blanket but wearable — designed to reduce anxiety and provide physical comfort during end-of-life care. Each gown is embroidered with the patient's chosen word or phrase on the interior collar, visible only to the wearer.

The Comfort Gown is the last garment many GLMZ residents ever wear. The tradition of the hidden embroidery began when a nurse noticed patients tracing the word on their collar with their fingers during their final hours — a private conversation between the wearer and the garment that holds them.
functionality: Anxiety reduction, comfort care, personal memorialization
what_it_says: This is the last thing someone chose to wrap around you, and there's a word against your throat that only you can read.
story_hooks: A Last Light Comfort Gown is found in a pawnshop with its hidden embroidery still intact — the word is a name, and the name belongs to someone who is still alive.

physical_description.visual_profile: A loose, draped garment that hangs softly from the shoulders, creating a gentle silhouette that neither clings nor overwhelms. The fabric pools slightly at the feet, suggesting weight and substance. Despite its medical purpose, it carries an unexpected dignity—more ritual wrap than hospital gown.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed and accommodating, designed to fit bodies in all states of rest and decline. The cut allows for easy movement of medical monitoring equipment and catheters without restriction. Gently oversized through the torso and arms, creating a cocoon-like embrace.
physical_description.primary_material: Weighted cotton-synthetic blend (60% organic cotton, 40% medical-grade polyester with distributed micro-bead interlayer). Soft to the touch but substantial, with micro-weighted particles sewn into quilted channels throughout the fabric.
physical_description.texture: Smooth outer surface with subtle quilting that creates gentle texture mapping. The weighted channels run vertically and horizontally, creating a grid pattern perceptible by touch. Inner collar is soft linen with embroidered thread—worn smooth from fingertips.
physical_description.color_scheme: Muted palette: dove gray, soft cream, or pale blue. Intentionally neutral and calming. Minimal branding—only a small Last Light Hospice insignia (Φ-licensed medical facility marker) on lower hem in matching thread.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic side snaps (medical staff can access without moving patient), positioned along the right seam. Soft fabric ties at the neck and back for gentle securing if needed, but never tight.
distinctive_features: Hidden embroidery on interior collar—patient's chosen word or phrase in thread matching their preferred color (visible only to wearer or intimate caregivers)
Quilted weight distribution channels (reduces pressure points unlike traditional weighted blankets)
Medical-grade seams reinforced for durability across hundreds of gentle wearings
Thermal regulation micro-fibers (maintain body heat without overheating)
Scent-infused option available (lavender, vanilla, or unscented—patient choice)
Flat-seam construction (no irritation against sensitive or augmentation-marked skin)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3/4 institutional care—not affordable for personal purchase, but provided as essential service within GLMZ hospice system. Signals access to dignified end-of-life care, which is paradoxically a marker of both social integration and mortality.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by the dying. The Last Light Comfort Gown has become a cultural artifact—a symbol of mercy in a world where augmentation and life-extension tech have made natural death both rare and precious. Wearing one means you've chosen or accepted your ending. Families sometimes keep them after, framed or folded in memory boxes.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when first given. As worn, develops a subtle softness through repeated gentle laundering. Over time, the embroidered collar becomes worn smooth and slightly frayed from constant fingering—each gown carries its wearer's final tactile conversation.
